jobs.description: IntroductionECO3 is a leading global supplier of integrated prepress solutions for the printing industry. Our solutions are designed to increase productivity, reduce costs, and promote sustainability throughout the print process.We are an international team with a positive mindset and a strong “can-do” attitude – committed to innovation, collaboration, and customer success.You print. We care.At this moment, we are looking for an Account Manager for the DACH & SEE region based in Germany.As Account Manager, you will be responsible for driving sales and building long-term client relationships while meeting revenue targets. within the Commercial Print Plates segment across the DACH region, primarily in Germany.- Focus on new business acquisition and market growth – identify opportunities, develop strategies, and execute them effectively.- Analyze and continuously improve sales processes and structures.- Prepare and follow up on quotations, customer meetings, presentations, and product demonstrations.- Work closely with technical and service teams to ensure outstanding customer support.- Regular travel activity across the DACH region (customer visits, trade fairs, industry events).Supporting the Sales Manager the commercial printing sector.- Analyze competitors and provide strategic feedback to internal stakeholders.- Represent ECO3 at trade shows, industry events, and customer visits.Your profileExperience & Qualifications- Several years of sales experience, ideally within the printing industry or related markets (prepress, consumables, print systems).- Solid technical understanding of commercial printing workflows and applications.- Proven ability to acquire new customers and build sustainable relationships.- Confident in using CRM systems and modern sales tools.- Skills & jobs.occupation: PhD positions - Statistical Physics and Active Matter - (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number ofPhD positions.- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department is headed by Ramin Golestanian and hosts a number of group leaders, postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.The researchThe PhD students will engage in theoretical and/or computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter, under the supervision of Ramin Golestanian. For more information concerning our current areas of research activity, visit our website (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp) ).Your profileWe are looking for excellent, enthusiastic and self-motivated early-career researchers with good communication skills to join our research team. The PhD candidate should have:- A Master’s degree (or comparable) in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;- Strong interest in nonequilibrium statistical physics and the physics of living systems across scales;- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.Our offerWe are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary and working hours are in accordance with the funding guidelines of the Max Planck Society for junior scientists. Working hours are fulltime; salary is 2/3 of E13 TVöD-Bund. Furthermore, we offer opportunities regarding work life balance as well as health promotion services. The PhD position is limited to three years. The starting date is flexible.The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. We encourage applications from women, especially in areas where they are underrepresented, which includes theoretical physics. Moreover, we are committed to providing suitable working environment for everyone including individuals with disabilities.Your applicationTo apply, please follow this link (https://jobs.b-ite.com/en/jobposting/64bbb9935c7fc269f86d9f96bf4a8e06636784110/apply)  and submit your CV, your academic records, a statement of your research interests, and contacts of two referees. Processing of applications will start after the deadline of 1st December 2026. While we may continue to receive applications until 1st April 2027, the positions will be filled as soon as suitable candidates are identified. Therefore, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.For questions, please contact:Prof. Dr. Ramin Golestanian Tel. +49 551 5176-100Email: golestanian-office@ds.mpg.de (https://mailto:golestanian-office@ds.mpg.de)  Max Planck Institute forDynamics and Self-OrganizationProf. Dr. Ramin GolestanianAm Faßberg 1737077 GöttingenGermanyErgänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Expertenkenntnisse: Physik, Theoretische Physik

The Department of Geriatrics at the University Medical Center Göttingen is seeking a highly motivated early-career postdoctoral researcher to join our interdisciplinary Heart & Brain research program.Our research focuses on ageing-related interactions between cardiovascular disease, brain health, delirium, cognitive decline and neurodegeneration. We combine deeply phenotyped clinical cohorts with molecular biomarkers, omics approaches and experimental models.The position is embedded in several ongoing translational research projects, including PAWEL/Bio-PAWEL, FINDERI, PRECOVERY and the DFG Research Training Group 2824 “Heart & Brain”, and offers the opportunity to work with established clinical cohorts, biosamples and molecular datasets.Your tasks- Bioinformatic and statistical analysis of molecular and omics datasets, including, for example, DNA methylation and miRNA data- Integration of molecular data with clinical, biomarker and longitudinal outcome data- Quality control, processing, analysis and reproducible documentation of both molecular and clinical datasets- Development and application of reproducible analysis workflows, primarily using R and/or Python- Functional annotation and pathway/network analyses and, where appropriate, integration of different molecular data layers- Contribution to experimental validation, including cell culture and molecular biology approaches- Scientific supervision and co-supervision of doctoral researchers, particularly within the DFG Research Training Group “Heart & Brain”- Preparation of scientific manuscripts, presentations and contributions to grant applications- Close collaboration with clinical researchers, molecular scientists, bioinformaticians and partner groups across the Göttingen CampusYour qualifications- PhD in bioinformatics, biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, neuroscience, biomedical sciences or a related discipline- Strong interest in translational research at the interface of clinical cohorts, molecular biomarkers and data science- Experience in the analysis of complex molecular or omics datasets- Proficiency in R and/or Python and sound knowledge of statistical data analysis- Experience with molecular biology and cell culture- Experience working in an S1 laboratory- Qualification or eligibility to act as a Biological Safety Officer (BBS) and/or project leader under German genetic engineering regulations would be an advantage, but is not mandatory- Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an interdisciplinary research team- Excellent written and spoken EnglishWe offer- The position provides the opportunity to work on clearly defined projects using existing, well-characterized cohorts and molecular datasets, with a strong perspective towards scientific publications within the funding period- You will join a collaborative translational research environment linking geriatrics, cardiovascular medicine, neuroscience, biomarker research and bioinformatics within the Heart & Brain research network at the Göttingen Campus- The position is particularly suited for an early postdoctoral researcher who wishes to strengthen their profile in translational biomarker research, computational analysis and the integration of experimental and clinical scienceApplications should include a short cover letter outlining your relevant methodological experience and research interests, a curriculum vitae including publications, relevant certificates, and contact details of two referees.

jobs.employer_name: Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen
jobs.description: Job posting no. 20261009The GWDG is seeking aStorage Expert (m/f/d)to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C) with a regular working week of 39 hours (100%). Remuneration is in accordance with the collective agreement for the German public service (federal government); depending on qualifications, the position will be grade TVöD E 13. The position is suitable for part-time work and initially limited till 31rd December 2029. The GWDG strives for long-term cooperation. If interested, there is the possibility of a doctorate.The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG operates the HLRN-IV system “Emmy”, one of the most powerful computers in the world.As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG offers technical support to researchers and students from various science domains using sophisticated computer codes, including earth system science, life science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. At the same time, we aim to improve our close collaboration with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), and specialized computing centers including the German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ) and the Institute for Advanced Simulation Jülich (IAS-JSC).As part of our AI Service Center for Sensitive and Critical Infrastructure (KISSKI) we have created a number of AI-based services that offer high levels of security and privacy due to being processed on our own hardware. The position will be located within the subproject “KISSKI-EvoKS” and closely collaborate with customers from SMEs and Startups to develop prototypes and workflows that lead to PoCs and Blueprints. Those customers will come predominantly from sectors with high data protection requirements.The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, AI, and Machine Learning.ResponsibilitiesWe have a wide range of potential responsibilities that we would like to discuss with you. Your responsibilities in our team could include, for example:- Design, implement, and optimize high-performance storage solutions tailored for AI and HPC workloads- Conduct research on scalable, cost-effective storage architectures suitable for AI training and HPC simulations in resource-constrained environments- Develop and deploy data management strategies for large-scale AI datasets, including data lifecycle management, versioning, backup, and security (e.g., GDPR-compliant data handling)- Investigate and prototype AI-optimized storage systems leveraging technologies such as NVMe, SSD caching, and distributed storage (e.g., Ceph, MinIO, Lustre)- Support SMEs in evaluating and selecting appropriate HPC and AI storage solutions- Collaborate with data scientists and engineers to ensure storage systems meet the demands of AI model training, inference, and real-time processing- Develop best practice guidelines and toolkits for SMEs to manage AI/HPC data efficiently and security- Provide technical advisory and training to SME teams on data storage, performance monitoring, and data governance- Monitor and benchmark storage performance, ensuring low latency, high throughput, and cost-efficiency for AI/HPC applicationsRequirements- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related field- Experience in HPC systems, storage infrastructure, and AI data engineering- Proven experience with high-performance storage technologies (e.g., Lustre, GPFS, Ceph, NFS, S3-compatible storage)- Strong knowledge of AI/ML data pipelines, including data ingestion, preprocessing, and model training workflows- Hands-on experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and orchestration tools in HPC/AI environments- Familiarity with cloud storage platforms- Experience in data lifecycle management, data versioning, and metadata management- Solid understanding of data security, privacy (GDPR), and compliance in AI applications- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills- Excellent communication skills and ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders- Very good German skills (C1)- Very good English skills (C1)- Willingness to travel on businessDesirable- Experience in research or innovation projects related to HPC, AI, or data infrastructure- Knowledge of AI-driven storage optimization (e.g., predictive data placement, auto-tiering)- Familiarity with open-source HPC/AI frameworks (e.g., Slurm, Singularity, MLflow, Kubeflow)- Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash) and system administration (Linux/UNIX)Our offer- Flexible working hours and opportunity for mobile working- A modern, diverse, and exceptional work environment with close proximity to academia and research at the intersection of several innovative technology sectors- An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center- Collaboration in a competent and committed team- Qualification and further development of your skills- Social benefits of the public sectorYour applicationHave we sparked your interest? Then please send us your application by 08.11.2026 via our online form:Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: About usAirbus ist Pionier einer nachhaltigen Luft- und Raumfahrt für eine sichere und vereinte Welt. Das Unternehmen arbeitet ständig an Innovationen für effiziente und technologisch fortschrittliche Lösungen in den Bereichen Luft- und Raumfahrt, Verteidigung sowie vernetzte Dienstleistungen. Im Bereich Hubschrauber stellt Airbus die weltweit effizientesten Lösungen und Dienstleistungen für zivile und militärische Hubschrauber bereit.Job descriptionIn order to support the Industrial System Evolution Team, Airbus Operations is looking for aWorking Student (d/f/m) in Single Aisle Industrial System EvolutionYou are a full time student, looking for a working student position and want to get to know the work of a project manager?  Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the major infrastructure and capacity expansion for the A320 Family in Hamburg as a working student (d/f/m) with approx. 18 hours a week!- Location: Hamburg- Start: 01.12.2026- Duration:  12 monthsYou will receive a collectively agreed salary of at least €18.53 per hour, depending on the job. There are also special payments such as vacation pay.Definition working studentWorking students are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. jobs.description: For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:Doctoral research associate for BabylAXO detector developmentLimited: 3 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: FHDO021/2026 | Deadline: 02.11.2026 | Full-time/Part‑time | Remote work possibleDESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.The Cluster of Excellence "Quantum Universe" performs research to understand mass and gravity at the interface between quantum physics and cosmology. The research team includes leading scientists from mathematics, particle physics, astrophysics, and cosmology at the University of Hamburg and DESY. As part of the cluster's experimental program to search for hypothetical very lightweight bosons, for example motivated by dark matter and dark energy in the universe, the construction of the BabylAXO experiment will start shortly. BabylAXO will look for axions and similar particles emitted by the sun in uncharted parameter regions. The doctoral research associate will engage in the start-up phase of BabylAXO and work on the extension of its scientific portfolio.The successful applicant will be attached to the ALPS group at DESY, which together with international partners is realizing new experimental facilities to search for new kinds of very lightweight elementary particles, works on new concepts targeting high-frequency gravitational waves and developing related technologies. Doctoral research associates will become members of the Quantum Universe Research School (QURS), which provides academic and key skills training, as well as career planning support. In addition, they will receive individual budgets to facilitate the attendance of summer schools and conferences, and to support other educational measures. Additional travel money for project-specific duties will be provided by the hosting research groups. Doctoral researchers may participate in teaching at the University and in the organization of the Cluster via an early career council.About your role:- Contribute to the commission and installation of the BabylAXO X-ray detection systems- Develop a calorimeter for BabylAXO sensitive to axions from solar fusion processes and supernova explosions- Explore synergies of the calorimeter development with medical applicationsAbout you:- MSc degree in Physics or equivalent qualification- Hands-on experience in the design, construction, commissioning, and operation of complex experimental setups- Programming experience in scientific computing environments- Independent, proactive, and goal-oriented working style with a strong commitment to solving complex technical challenges- Excellent written and spoken English skills- Experience in detector development for or operation of experimental particle physics or dark matter search experimentsGood reasons to join:Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus.
